turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on comparatives (-er, more ... than)?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: short words add -er (easy - easier); long words use more; then than.
Right: "A horse is heavier than a dog." Wrong: "A horse is heavyer than a dog." The wrong one keeps the y; a short adjective ending in y changes it to i before -er.
Let me think aloud with one example: "A tiger is more dangerous than a cat." Step 1: dangerous is a long adjective. Step 2: so I put more in front of it. Step 3: then than, and the second thing.
Now your turn. Start with step 1, then complete the sentence:
Complete: "Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."

Here is one example with a different word: hot ends in one vowel plus one consonant, so the final consonant doubles before -er: hot - hotter.
